correctness.rationale: For all d>=2, the known complete facet normals have Euclidean lengths sqrt2 and sqrt(k(d-k)/d). The strictly positive explicit Dirichlet path Green matrix yields a sharp upper bound on any inball radius from the first coordinate, with parabolic deficit vector attaining it. The first Green row strictly positive proves center uniqueness. Exact facet distances prove contact classification; antipodal monotone permutations and strictly convex squared norm prove unique circumcenter and exclusively vertex contacts. Standard-library 23044 checks and separate 31 linear programs confirm, but do not replace, the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The result completely identifies the unique Euclidean inball and exactly which facets touch it throughout a natural infinite family. The bounded-radius/large-circumsphere separation shows a genuine asymptotic shape collapse compared with the full permutahedron sharing its outer sphere, despite unchanged cubical combinatorics. Both precise contact spectrum and uniqueness require a nontrivial sharp Green-kernel argument; neither a generic trivial normalization nor a finite unmotivated computation.
